A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Self-MoE/MiXSE work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, generalization tests, and statistical results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons, component ablations, and the repeated-run analysis.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 retain the same synthetic-data generation, LoRA experts, top-k linear router, and router-only optimization. The appendix generation prompts are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four target benchmarks and seven non-target benchmarks, covering knowledge, reasoning, mathematics, coding, commonsense, and truthfulness. Training-data sources and represented tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods, including self-specialized models, instance merging, TIES, DARE, and the literature comparisons in Table 7. DEMix is newly discussed but is not added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Few-shot settings, model variants, dataset sizes, and Appendix A training settings remain unchanged. v2 emphasizes both MMLU settings, but the 5-shot comparison already appears in v1 Table 7. Parameter-count additions document existing configurations.

E4.justification: The router ablations, routing analysis, generalization tests, data/expert scaling studies, and seed-only experiment are retained. Appendix C.2 becomes D.2. New Section 4.8 discusses overhead without adding an overhead experiment.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix C.3 and v2 Appendix D.3 report the same three runs with different few-shot example lists, standard deviations, and p-value of 0.03 for MiXSE versus instance merging.

E6.justification: Benchmark scores, ablation outcomes, plotted trends, and appendix statistical results are unchanged. Table 1 retains averages of 47.8 for the base model and 54.3 for MiXSE. Added parameter columns provide configuration information without new task-performance outcomes.

T1.justification: The formal problem mapping, LoRA factorization, mixture equations, routing weights, and training objective are mathematically unchanged. No theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added.

C1.justification: The claims about modular self-improvement, specialization trade-offs, efficiency, and applicability across models are retained. The new contribution bullets and abstract's 6.5-percentage-point figure summarize claims and results already present in v1.

C2.justification: New Section 4.8 explains overhead through sparse activation and lightweight experts, contrasting their memory requirements with conventional MoEs. v2 also explains the preference for zero-shot MMLU and newly acknowledges that XLoRA implementation optimization was not investigated.

D1.justification: v2 adds active/total parameter documentation and explicitly states that comparison models use LoRA. It removes v1's prospective code-release statement and dataset-license information. The prompts, hyperparameters, software, hardware, and training-time disclosures otherwise remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds DEMix to its semantic-expert positioning, cites Dettmers et al. and Lin et al. for the MMLU rationale, and Chung et al. for multitask tuning. The Self-Specialization citation changes from preprint to publication without introducing a different work.

P1.justification: v2 adds explicit contribution bullets, edits the abstract and several passages, introduces an overhead subsection, and relocates limitations and benchmark descriptions to the appendices. Most methodological and experimental prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column layout, extensively repositioning and resizing figures and tables and changing caption placement. Tables 1, 5, and 7 gain parameter columns. The existing five figures and twelve tables are retained.

improvement.justification: The parameter accounting, MMLU rationale, and explicit XLoRA limitation make efficiency claims and evaluation choices easier to assess. These provide modest clarity gains while the scientific results remain unchanged. Removing dataset-license details and the prospective code-release statement partly offsets the improved documentation.
